newsitem.title: USA: Interstate to buy back shares from Ralston.
newsitem.headline: Interstate to buy back shares from Ralston.

text.p: Interstate Bakeries Corp (IBC) said Thursday it will repurchase one million shares of its common stock from Ralston Purina Co.
Ralston had acquired the shares in connection with the sale of its Continental Baking Co subsidiary to IBC in July 1995.

The two companies said Thursday they filed a registration statement with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission for Ralston to possibly offer up to $360 million, plus a $40 million over-allotment option, in Stock Appreciation Income Linked Securities (SAILS).
The SAILS are exchangeable notes of Ralston which upon maturity would be exchanged for shares of IBC common stock owned by Ralston or for cash, as decided by Ralston.

The SAILS would be issued in late June or July, the companies said, at the price then of IBC stock. The issuance is subject to the registration statements and final approval by the executive and finance committees of Ralston's board of directors, Ralston said.

The companies said the underwriters for the proposed offering will be a group led by Credit Suisse First Boston. Bear, Stearns & Co Inc, J.P. Morgan Securities Inc, Lehman Brothers Inc and Salomon Brothers Inc will be co-managers.
Ralston, which produces pet and livestock feed, batteries, and protein products, currently owns a 45 percent stake in IBC.
IBC bakes and distribute fresh bakery in the United States under brand names such as Wonder, Hostess and Home Pride.
